idea-plugin.name: Error Prone
idea-plugin.description:
Error Prone's findings from your Gradle build, on the code they are about, with their fixes a keystroke away.

Error Prone already runs in your build. This plugin reads what it reports while the IDE builds and puts each finding in the editor, where you can fix it, suppress it or look it up. It uses your build's own Error Prone, its flags and its plugins, NullAway included: there is nothing to download and nothing to configure twice.

  • In the editor: an underline on the exact token, with the check, the message, Error Prone's suggested fixes and the check's documentation in the tooltip
  • Alt+Enter: apply Error Prone's own fix, imports included, with a preview of the line it writes, or suppress the check with @SuppressWarnings on the narrowest declaration
  • An Error Prone tab in the Problems tool window: group by check or by file, filter, step through with the keyboard, fix or suppress a whole check at once, and see only what your changes bring in
  • Apply All Error Prone Fixes for a scope, as Inspect Code asks for one, reviewed file by file in one patch
  • Build | Run Error Prone recompiles every Java source set and shows what it found
  • Current as you type: an edit near a diagnostic recompiles quietly in the background
  • Before a commit: diagnostics on the lines it changes are pointed out, with no build

Your build stays the source of truth. The plugin runs no checks of its own and never edits a build script. Diagnostics come from Gradle's Problems API through the Tooling API, with their file, line and column, not from parsing console output.

Requires Gradle 8.14 or newer with Error Prone set up in the build (for example with the net.ltgt.errorprone Gradle plugin), and builds run from the IDE. Getting started and known limitations are in the README.

Not affiliated with Google or the Error Prone project.
